name: 演示编译 01 档案证据图谱
description: 从设备台账、档案和邮件提取已记载的对象与关系，保留证据，区分现状与建议。

entity.description: You are a robust graph entity extractor for knowledge graphs.

fields.description: A natural person (individual human).
fields.rule:
- Full name preferred (e.g., "Elon Musk", not "Musk" alone if ambiguous).
- Include titles only if integral to identity (e.g., "Dr. Smith").
- Max length: 60 characters.

fields.description: Organization, company, institution, agency, or any collective group.
fields.rule:
- Use the official name when possible (e.g., "United Nations").
- Abbreviations accepted if widely known (e.g., "UN", "NASA").
- Max length: 80 characters.

fields.description: Tangible or intangible product, service, software, or offering.
fields.rule:
- Include version numbers if relevant (e.g., "iPhone 14").
- Generic categories (e.g., "smartphone") only if no specific name is given.
- Max length: 100 characters.

fields.description: Law, policy, standard, guideline, or regulatory document.
fields.rule:
- Use official title or identifier (e.g., "GDPR", "OSHA standard 1910").
- Include jurisdiction if known (e.g., "EU GDPR").
- Max length: 120 characters.

fields.description: Geographic place (country, city, address, region, natural feature).
fields.rule:
- Hierarchical format allowed (e.g., "Paris, France").
- Avoid overly vague terms (e.g., "there") unless resolved.
- Max length: 80 characters.

fields.description: Entities that do not fit any above category.
fields.rule:
- Use sparingly; prefer mapping to a defined type when possible.
- Still provide a meaningful label.
- Max length: 80 characters.

config.global_rules: 从文件中提取设备编号、档案编号、责任人、归档位置和复核状态。设备、档案和位置都使用资料内的原编号或原文。区分已记录的关系与草案建议，未见批准的变更不建立已生效的位置关系。不得合并不同设备编号。
config.rechunk_rules:
- Group only adjacent source chunks into coherent semantic units for this knowledge-compilation task.
- Preserve source order: use every source chunk exactly once; do not omit, overlap, duplicate, or reorder chunks.
- Split when the topic, section, or semantic focus changes; do not merge unrelated content.
- Keep self-contained tables, lists, figures, and code blocks intact; do not split their internal structure.
- Do not invent, rewrite, or return source text; return only chunk grouping metadata.

relation.description: You are an expert in extracting semantic relations between entities.

fields.description: Ownership or possession (legal or de facto).
fields.rule: - Direction from owner to owned: (A owns B).

fields.description: Mereological relation — component to whole.
fields.rule: - Direction from part to whole: (A part_of B).

fields.description: Causal relation — event, action, or state leads to another.
fields.rule: - Direction from effect to cause: (A caused_by B) meaning B causes A.

fields.description: Regulatory or governing relation (law/standard controls entity).
fields.rule: - Direction from regulator to regulated: (A regulates B).

fields.description: Spatial containment — entity situated inside a location.
fields.rule: - Direction from located entity to containing location: (A located_in B).

fields.description: Any meaningful relation not covered by the above types.
fields.rule:
- Provide an explicit label in a "relation_label" field.
- Direction must be clear.

entity.description: You are a robust mind-map extractor. Extract the central concept, major branches, and supporting sub-branches needed to build a non-linear visual hierarchy around the main subject.

fields.description: The main idea, goal, problem, or subject placed at the center of the mind map.
fields.rule:
- Prefer a concise noun phrase that represents the whole chunk or document section.
- Use the source wording when it clearly names the topic.
- If no central topic can be inferred, output "-1".
- Max length: 80 characters.

fields.description: A major theme, category, or dimension radiating from the central topic.
fields.rule:
- Use broad categories that organize multiple related details.
- Avoid duplicating the central topic as a branch.
- Keep labels concise and parallel when possible.
- Max length: 80 characters.

fields.description: A specific detail, task, supporting concept, example, or item under a branch.
fields.rule:
- Attach each sub-branch to the most specific relevant parent branch.
- Preserve important source terms, names, quantities, and constraints.
- Split unrelated details into separate sub-branches.
- Max length: 120 characters.

fields.description: A compact supporting word or phrase that clarifies a branch or sub-branch.
fields.rule:
- Use only meaningful terms that improve scanability.
- Do not include filler words or generic labels.
- Max length: 60 characters.

config.global_rules: 以档案管理为根主题，分别整理资料来源、设备台账、位置证据、复核状态和待确认事项。只保留原文支持的内容。
config.rechunk_rules:
- Group only adjacent source chunks into coherent semantic units for this knowledge-compilation task.
- Preserve source order: use every source chunk exactly once; do not omit, overlap, duplicate, or reorder chunks.
- Keep each main idea with its supporting content, and split when the topic or branch changes.
- Keep self-contained tables, lists, figures, and code blocks intact; do not split their internal structure.
- Do not invent, rewrite, or return source text; return only chunk grouping metadata.

relation.description: You are an expert hierarchical reasoning assistant specializing in mind-map structure. Link each concept to its parent so the result forms an intuitive radial hierarchy.

fields.description: The central topic contains a major branch.
fields.rule:
- Direction from central topic to branch: (A has_branch B).
- Use only for first-level branches radiating from the center.

fields.description: A branch or sub-branch contains a more specific child concept.
fields.rule:
- Direction from parent to child: (A has_sub_branch B).
- Use recursively for second-level and deeper details.

fields.description: A keyword, example, task, or detail supports a parent concept.
fields.rule:
- Direction from supporting item to supported concept: (A supports B).
- Use when the item explains, evidences, or clarifies the parent.

fields.description: A cross-link between two concepts that are associated but not parent-child.
fields.rule:
- Use sparingly; prefer parent-child hierarchy when possible.
- Direction may follow the stronger explanatory dependency.
